glossary.Chronic hyperglycaemia: Blood glucose that stays too high over months to years, damaging nerves and small vessels.
glossary.Hyperglycaemia: Blood glucose that is higher than normal.
glossary.Distal: Further from the centre of the body, such as the feet and hands.
glossary.Glycaemic control: How well blood glucose is kept within target, usually judged by HbA1c.
glossary.Polyneuropathy: Damage to many peripheral nerves at once, usually symmetrical and starting in the feet.
glossary.Bilateral: Affecting both sides of the body.
glossary.Tuning fork: A metal fork that vibrates when struck, placed on bony points to test vibration sense.
glossary.Light touch: Sensation tested with cotton wool, carried by large sensory nerve fibres.
glossary.Foot ulcers: Open sores on the foot that heal poorly, often over pressure points in a numb foot.
glossary.Vagal: Relating to the vagus nerve, which controls gut movement and slows the heart.
glossary.Bladder dysfunction: Problems emptying or controlling the bladder, such as retention or incontinence.
glossary.Cranial nerve palsy: Weakness or paralysis of a muscle supplied by one of the twelve cranial nerves.
glossary.Protective sensation: Enough feeling in the feet to notice pain from injury before damage occurs.
glossary.Ulceration: Formation of an open sore where the skin has broken down.
glossary.Peripheral arterial disease: Narrowing of the leg arteries by atherosclerosis, reducing blood flow and slowing healing.
glossary.PAD: Peripheral arterial disease: narrowed leg arteries that reduce blood supply to the feet.
glossary.Amputation: Surgical removal of a limb or part of a limb.
glossary.Limb-threatening: Serious enough to risk losing the limb if not treated urgently.
glossary.Clinical diagnosis: A diagnosis made from history and examination without needing a confirmatory test.
glossary.Neuropathic pain: Pain caused by damaged nerves, often burning, shooting or tingling.
glossary.Contraindicated: Should not be used because it could cause harm in that patient.
glossary.SNRI: Serotonin-noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor, such as duloxetine, used for depression and nerve pain.
glossary.Gabapentinoid: Drug class including gabapentin and pregabalin that calms overactive nerve signalling.
glossary.Pain management clinic: A specialist service for pain that does not respond to standard treatment.
glossary.Mobilisation measures: Steps to reduce dizziness on standing, such as rising slowly and staying active.
glossary.Osmotic stress: Cell damage from water being drawn in by a build-up of solutes such as sorbitol.
glossary.Oxidative stress: Damage to cells by reactive oxygen molecules when antioxidant defences are overwhelmed.
glossary.Fructose: A sugar made from sorbitol in the polyol pathway.
glossary.Microvascular: Relating to the smallest blood vessels, such as capillaries.
glossary.Ischaemia: Inadequate blood supply to a tissue, starving it of oxygen.
glossary.Nerve conduction: The passage of electrical signals along a nerve.
glossary.Sympathetic: Part of the autonomic nervous system that tightens blood vessels and raises heart rate.
glossary.Vasomotor: Controlling the narrowing and widening of blood vessels.
glossary.Autonomic fibres: Nerve fibres that control automatic functions like blood pressure, gut movement and bladder.
glossary.Pelvic autonomic fibres: Autonomic nerves supplying the bladder and genitals.
